This correction is reflected in the committed migration file itself, not merely applied out-of-band — the file on disk and the live database now match exactly. entries.evidenceSource: Direct live application via the exact-file direct-SQL mechanism (.tmp-run-migration.cjs, same pg pooler connection used for 66-76) executing supabase/migrations/77_resident_workforce_claim.sql against the live database. Preflight (read-only) confirmed claim_workforce_member(uuid,text) did not already exist live, and confirmed the live verify_resident_login body matched migration 64 exactly (no pre-77 drift) before applying. IMPORTANT DISCLOSED FINDING, SELF-CAUGHT AND CORRECTED DURING LIVE TESTING, BEFORE recording VERIFIED_APPLIED: the first live apply used a version of claim_workforce_member whose RETURNS TABLE clause named its OUT parameters tenant_id/workforce_id/is_workforce_member/is_tenant_admin/status/claimed_at — plain PL/pgSQL implicitly declares each RETURNS TABLE column name as an OUT-parameter variable for the whole function body, and every one of those names collides with a REAL organisation_memberships column referenced inside the function. The first live security test run failed immediately on 'authenticated valid claim succeeds' with Postgres error 'column reference "tenant_id" is ambiguous'. A first fix attempt (aliasing every table reference — workforce w, organisation_memberships om — and qualifying every WHERE/SELECT/COALESCE reference) was applied live and RE-FAILED WITH THE IDENTICAL ERROR on retest: a dedicated raw-pg diagnostic (SET LOCAL request.jwt.claims + SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated inside a BEGIN...ROLLBACK, bypassing supabase-js's less detailed error wrapping) pinpointed the true ambiguity source as the INSERT statement's own target column list, a SQL position that cannot be alias-qualified at all — proving the alias-only fix was structurally insufficient, not merely incomplete. The correct fix (applied second, live): renamed every RETURNS TABLE OUT-parameter column to a claim_-prefixed form (claim_tenant_id/claim_workforce_id/claim_is_workforce_member/claim_is_tenant_admin/claim_status/claim_claimed_at; membership_id needed no change since no real column is named exactly that), which removes the collision entirely, and added DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS claim_workforce_member(uuid, text) immediately before the CREATE OR REPLACE (Postgres refuses to change an existing function's RETURNS TABLE column shape in place — the same precedent already established by migration 64). The corrected file on disk and the live database now match exactly; src/modules/auth/lib/organisationMembershipService.ts's ClaimWorkforceMemberResult interface was updated to the same renamed shape (npx tsc --noEmit clean). Post-apply STRUCTURAL verification: pg_proc confirms claim_workforce_member exists, prosecdef=true, search_path=public pinned. Effective-live-privilege verification (the migration-76 lesson applied prospectively, before any live test ran): information_schema.routine_privileges confirms EXECUTE granted to exactly authenticated, postgres, service_role — no anon entry, no bare PUBLIC entry; information_schema.role_table_grants on organisation_memberships confirms authenticated still holds SELECT only (no new INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grant was introduced by this migration); pg_policies on organisation_memberships confirms still exactly the one migration-76 SELECT-own policy, unchanged. verify_resident_login's live post-apply definition was re-pulled and confirmed to differ from its migration-64 baseline by exactly one added clause (AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM organisation_memberships om WHERE om.workforce_id = w.id AND om.legacy_code_disabled_at IS NOT NULL)) — every prior clause preserved character-for-character, LANGUAGE sql (not rewritten to plpgsql, so this function carries none of the OUT-parameter collision risk). LIVE SECURITY/CONCURRENCY/LEGACY-GUARD VERIFICATION using DISPOSABLE SYNTHETIC Supabase Auth users (created/deleted via the service-role admin API, throwaway passwords this session set itself) plus disposable synthetic tenant/workforce fixtures (created/deleted via direct SQL), all removed in a finally block and independently re-confirmed absent afterward via a separate read-only pass (0 leftover synthetic tenants, workforce rows, memberships linked to any synthetic workforce row, and 0 leftover synthetic auth users): proved live and end-to-end, 0 failures across every required case — unauthenticated and anon-key-only claims rejected; wrong resident code rejected; inactive workforce rejected; authenticated valid claim succeeds with tenant correctly derived from the workforce row (never caller-supplied), is_workforce_member=true, correct workforce_id, claimed_at set, claim_method='resident_code_claim', legacy_code_disabled_at remains null; an existing tenant-admin membership gains is_workforce_member=true on the same row while its pre-existing is_tenant_admin=true survives untouched (never in the DO UPDATE SET list); a same-user/same-workforce repeat claim succeeds idempotently (no second row created, claimed_at/claim_method COALESCE-preserved, not overwritten); the same user cannot silently switch that tenant membership to a different workforce row (rejected, original workforce_id confirmed unchanged); a different authenticated user cannot claim a workforce row already linked to an active membership (rejected via migration 76's own partial unique index); one auth user can legitimately claim distinct workforce identities in two different tenants (two independent membership rows, not merged); workforce.doctor_id was independently re-confirmed null on every claimed workforce row throughout — never written by this RPC. CONCURRENCY: both required races were exercised and the database's own atomicity (not application-level inference) was proven to leave exactly one canonical winner in each case — same auth user + same tenant + two different workforce rows simultaneously (exactly one claim succeeded, one canonical membership row remained); two different auth users + the same workforce row simultaneously (exactly one claim succeeded, the workforce row ended linked to exactly one authenticated membership, never both, never silently overwritten). LEGACY LOGIN GUARD, all 5 required cases proved with disposable synthetic data only (no real resident code was read, recovered, or exposed): (A) no membership at all — valid legacy resident code still works; (B) a claimed membership with legacy_code_disabled_at IS NULL — valid legacy login still works; (C) a claimed membership with an explicit synthetic legacy_code_disabled_at IS NOT NULL (set via direct privileged fixture SQL — no production code path in this slice ever sets this column) — legacy login correctly fails (0 rows); (D) clearing that synthetic marker restores expected legacy behavior; (E) wrong code and inactive workforce continue to be rejected exactly as before, unchanged. REGRESSION verification (structural + live, matching migration 76's own discipline): node scripts/verify-migration-77.cjs (38/38, including 3 checks added specifically for the DROP FUNCTION insertion and OUT-parameter rename), node scripts/verify-migration-76.cjs, scripts/verify-resident-email-login.cjs, scripts/verify-resident-home.cjs, scripts/verify-my-assignment.cjs, scripts/verify-full-roster.cjs, scripts/verify-roster-revisions.cjs, and npm run verify (typecheck+build) were all re-run and confirm every existing surface remains unaffected — 3 checks in verify-migration-76.cjs and 1 check in verify-resident-home.cjs report an expected, benign, unrelated stale self-check (each script's own hardcoded 'migration ceiling is exactly 75/76' and/or 'git status on migrations|src shows nothing since that task' assertion, written before migration 77 existed, invalidated by migration 77's mere existence/prior commit rather than by any regression in the surfaces those scripts actually test); every other check in both scripts passes, and no other script showed any failure of any kind.

entries.evidenceSource: Direct live application via the exact-file direct-SQL mechanism (.tmp-run-migration.cjs, same pg pooler connection used for 66-77) executing supabase/migrations/78_resident_get_current_assignment_authenticated_membership.sql against the live database. Preflight (read-only) confirmed _resident_authenticated_membership_match did not already exist live (0 rows), and confirmed the live resident_get_current_assignment body matched migration 72 exactly, byte for byte, before applying. IMPORTANT DISCLOSED FINDING, SELF-CAUGHT DURING THIS DEPLOYMENT REVIEW'S OWN INTERNAL-HELPER-PRIVILEGE CHECK, BEFORE the first live apply (not a live-testing-surfaced bug like migrations 76/77's, but the same ambient-default-privilege lesson applied prospectively on explicit inspection): the migration file as locally implemented only REVOKEd EXECUTE on _resident_authenticated_membership_match from PUBLIC and anon, not authenticated. Since this project's ambient ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES grants EXECUTE directly to authenticated (not merely via PUBLIC) at function-creation time — the exact migration-76 lesson — an authenticated (non-anon) client could have called this internal-only helper directly via PostgREST, bypassing resident_get_current_assignment's own workforce-active check and structural precedence, to probe membership state for an arbitrary workforce_id. Corrected before the first live apply: added an explicit REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION _resident_authenticated_membership_match(uuid) FROM authenticated, by role name, matching the other two explicit revokes (never inferred from each other). scripts/verify-migration-78.cjs's grant check was updated to require all three explicit revokes. Post-apply STRUCTURAL verification: pg_proc confirms the helper exists, prosecdef=false (NOT SECURITY DEFINER, matching this repo's own precedent for small helpers — _normalize_supervision_name/_roster_section_fallbacks/_resolve_workforce_names), search_path=public pinned. EFFECTIVE-LIVE-PRIVILEGE VERIFICATION (both information_schema.routine_privileges AND the more rigorous, ACL-independent has_function_privilege()): the helper's EXECUTE grants are exactly {postgres, service_role} — confirmed via has_function_privilege('anon', ..., 'EXECUTE')=false and has_function_privilege('authenticated', ..., 'EXECUTE')=false, proving the correction closed the gap rather than merely asserting it from source text. resident_get_current_assignment's own grants (anon, authenticated, PUBLIC, postgres, service_role) are confirmed byte-for-byte unchanged from the pre-78 preflight snapshot. organisation_memberships' table grants and its single SELECT-own policy are confirmed unchanged from the migration-76/77 baseline — this migration adds no new write path, reading that table only via the existing SECURITY DEFINER context of resident_get_current_assignment. A pg_get_functiondef pull of the live post-apply resident_get_current_assignment body confirms it matches the migration file exactly, including the new structural-precedence credential block; resident_get_current_full_roster, resident_get_roster_section_presentation, resident_set_email, verify_resident_login, verify_chief_login, claim_workforce_member, and current_user_organisation_memberships were all independently re-confirmed to still exist post-apply (untouched by this migration, which never references any of them in actual SQL, confirmed structurally by scripts/verify-migration-78.cjs). LIVE SYNTHETIC AUTHORIZATION MATRIX (disposable synthetic Supabase Auth users, 2 tenants, 9 workforce rows, 8 memberships, and one real published-roster fixture with a genuine GOP-grid match — all created via the service-role admin API / direct SQL as postgres, bypassing RLS — removed in a finally block and independently re-verified absent afterward via a separate read-only pass across both this test round and a later UX-walkthrough round: 0 leftover tenants/workforce/collections/settings/auth users in both sweeps): 0 failures across all 20 required cases — authenticated claimed active resident succeeds with p_code=NULL; the same succeeds even when p_code is a deliberately WRONG string, proving the strong path is evaluated unconditionally first and never inspects the code once it matches; the same authenticated user is rejected when requesting an unrelated workforce row with no valid code; a multi-tenant user (independent active memberships in two different tenants) accesses each tenant's own workforce correctly and is rejected for an unrelated third workforce row; a tenant-admin-only membership (workforce_id IS NULL) never authorizes any resident-workforce request; suspended and revoked memberships each independently fail to authorize the strong path (falling through to a legacy check that also correctly rejects, since no valid code was supplied); an inactive workforce is rejected via both the strong path (helper requires workforce active=true) and the unchanged legacy path; a legacy-only resident (zero organisation_memberships rows at all) succeeds with the valid code and fails with a wrong code; a claimed-but-not-personally-matching workforce with legacy_code_disabled_at IS NULL still allows an unauthenticated caller with the valid code through (unchanged pre-78 behavior); the same workforce with legacy_code_disabled_at IS NOT NULL correctly blocks that unauthenticated legacy attempt; a DIFFERENT membership with an ACTIVE matching authenticated session AND legacy_code_disabled_at IS NOT NULL on that same row still succeeds via the strong path, proving disabling the weak path never disables the strong path; anon (no Supabase Auth session at all) cannot exploit the new path (strong path skipped, legacy path rejects a null code) and cannot call the internal helper directly via PostgREST (EXECUTE revoked) — independently, an AUTHENTICATED (non-anon) caller was also confirmed unable to call the helper directly via PostgREST, proving the authenticated-revoke correction actually took effect live, not merely in source text; an extra, unrecognized p_tenant_id argument is rejected outright by PostgREST's own schema-cache lookup (no such parameter exists on any signature), positively confirming no caller-supplied tenant authority exists; the returned status/month/year/assignments payload for the same real GOP-grid match was confirmed byte-for-byte identical between the strong-path (authenticated) and legacy-path (code) callers. ONE HONEST, DISCLOSED FINDING (not a failure, not fixed, and not something migration 78 is designed to change): an authenticated User A who supplies an UNRELATED workforce's own valid, non-disabled legacy code still receives that workforce's data via the legacy fallback — this is unchanged, pre-existing 'the code is the credential, independent of who supplies it' behavior (already true since migration 67), gated exclusively by that specific workforce's own legacy_code_disabled_at, and is not a new capability or regression introduced here.
